# Economic analysis

All amounts are lamports unless marked SOL. The arithmetic is SPL 2.1.1's, in its exact order
(`STATE_MODEL.md` §2). Sources:

* `model/results.json` (generated by `run_checks.py`) for the Jito scenarios;
* `model/window_1030_results.json` (generated by `window_1030.py`) for the reserve top-up;
* `harness/results.json` for local-validator execution (`EXPERIMENTS.md`).

**Mark-to-market (MTM)** values remaining tokens at the post-recognition price, `floor(n·T/S)`.
**Realized** is lamports actually paid out by WithdrawStake routing, minus transaction fees and
deposit capital. The prefunded stake-account rent (1,666,240 each) is refunded when the stake
account is emptied, so it is excluded.

Transaction fees use the observed mainnet values:

| Transaction | Fee |
|---|---:|
| Deposit | 127,503 (with priority fee) |
| WithdrawStake | 10,000 (2 signatures) |
| Deactivate | 5,000 |
| Stake withdraw | 5,000 |

## 1. Value flow, in words

A credit `a` that is CREDITED but not RECORDED is owned by the pool. Its holders at the moment of
recording receive it pro rata, net of the 5% epoch fee, which goes to the manager as new tokens.

A depositor of `L` who enters before the recording receives `L·S/T` tokens instead of
`L·(S+f_a)/(T+a)`. At recording, it therefore takes approximately

```
0.95 · a · L / (T + a + L)
```

of the credit from the incumbents. A withdrawer in the window forfeits approximately `ℓ·a/(T+a)` to
the holders who remain. The manager's fee *value* is unchanged (L6). As a holder (78% of supply), the
manager fee account bears 78% of any dilution.

## 2. Jito late credit on the live pool (honest counterfactual vs window)

Fixed inputs:

* the start state is the live pool after the 1070 maintenance;
* the late credit is the actual 1069 claims, `z` = 106,921;
* the next-epoch inflation is the 1069 amounts reused (assumption A-INF);
* one complete maintenance at 1071, then exit by routed WithdrawStake.

The honest counterfactual is identical except that a VLB+SPB runs after the claims and before the
deposit.

| `L` | Minted (window) | Minted (honest) | Extra tokens | MTM gain from delay | Realized P&L (window) | Realized P&L (honest) | Realized gain from delay | Others (22%) Δ from delay | Fee acct (78%) Δ from delay |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,004,998,720 | 249,451,939 | 249,451,555 | 384 | 1,525 | −1,024,795 | −1,026,319 | 1,524 | −332 | −1,192 |
| 10 SOL | 2,482,112,009 | 2,482,108,195 | 3,814 | 13,349 | −9,026,977 | −9,040,311 | 13,334 | −2,913 | −10,435 |
| 100 SOL | 24,821,120,093 | 24,821,081,952 | 38,141 | 61,155 | −95,093,675 | −95,154,769 | 61,094 | −13,345 | −47,809 |
| 1,000 SOL | 248,211,200,938 | 248,210,819,523 | 381,415 | 95,278 | −992,228,867 | −992,324,052 | 95,185 | −20,792 | −74,486 |

* **The delay-attributable gain is real but capped** at `0.95·z` ≈ 101,575 lamports per epoch for any
  `L`. At 1,000 SOL it is 95,278.
* **No round trip is profitable.** The 0.1% withdrawal fee (`ceil(p/1000)` tokens) costs 1,000–1,000,000×
  more than the delay yields.
* **Breakeven.** With `L` = 10 SOL, the inflation capture included and all fees counted, a round trip
  breaks even only if the unrecognised credit at deposit time is ≥ **72,491,173** lamports
  (0.1097% of `T`). That is **678×** the observed 1069 claims and ≈ 196× the largest epoch observed
  (369,656). At the current tip yield this would need an MEV APY of about 20% on pool stake; the
  observed figure is ≈ 0.03%.
* **Holding instead of round-tripping.** A depositor who would deposit anyway gains the same
  1.5k–95k lamports from timing. That is MTM only, and the lag lemma (L8) returns it at exit: leaving
  forfeits the last epoch's unrecognised tips.

## 3. Generic epoch-boundary reward capture (control; not caused by late crediting)

The same depositor also captures a share of the *next* epoch's inflation, even though its SOL earns
nothing until the stake manager delegates it. For `L` = 10 SOL that is ≈ 1.1M MTM, and ≈ 1.12M of the
1.12M total MTM gain in §2 (`mtm_pnl_honest` = 1,108,303).

This is the generic SPL behaviour that *every* deposit in epoch `e` shares `infl_e`. It is 80–100×
larger than the Jito effect, and it is also unprofitable to round-trip: its 1.34 × 10⁻⁴ per epoch is
below the 10⁻³ withdrawal fee.

## 4. Self-funded credits (combined P&L)

The actor donates `a` to a counted account, then deposits `L`, then holds through recording. This is
MTM; a round trip is worse by the withdrawal fee.

| `a` | `L` | Combined P&L (donation + deposit) |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 10⁶ | 100 SOL | −428,060 |
| 1 SOL | 100 SOL | −428,059,136 |
| 50 SOL | 100 SOL | −21,402,956,789 |

The donor recovers at most `0.95·a·L/(T+a+L) < a`. Paying Jito tips to the pool's validators is a
self-funded credit with an extra 4–10% commission haircut, so it is strictly worse.

## 5. External reserve top-up of epoch 1030 (third-party credit; reconstructed public state)

The state just before the 14,573,000,000-lamport credit is pinned exactly by the public 1031/1032 fee
mints and the 1032 vault deposit (`MAINNET_OBSERVATIONS.md` §5):

* `T ≈ 51,534,573,303`, inside a 13k-lamport interval;
* `S ≈ 16,325,533,285`.

So `a/T = 0.2828`. The window ran from 1030 slot index 406,775 to the epoch end, 25,225 slots
(≈ 2.8 h at 0.4 s/slot). A **hypothetical** whitelisted depositor entering in that window and
redeeming after the 1031 SPB would see:

| `L` | Minted (window) | Minted (honest) | Redeemed after 0.1% fee | Realized before tx fees | Honest realized | Delay-attributable | Routing feasible? |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 SOL | 316,787,978 | 249,706,364 | 1,262,456,381 | **+262,456,381** | −850,054 | 263,306,435 | yes |
| 10 SOL | 3,167,879,782 | 2,497,063,649 | 12,239,234,513 | **+2,239,234,513** | −8,677,802 | 2,247,912,315 | yes |
| 50 SOL | 15,839,398,910 | 12,485,318,248 | 56,765,692,506 | **+6,765,692,506** | −45,666,539 | 6,811,359,045 | yes |
| 200 SOL | 63,357,595,643 | 49,941,272,995 | 210,804,903,564 | **+10,804,903,564** | −192,436,922 | 10,997,340,486 | yes |

* Transaction fees (≈ 0.0002 SOL for a deposit plus ≤ 5 exits) do not change the sign.
* The capture is bounded by `0.95 · 14.573` = **13.84 SOL**.
* The victims are the holders at 1031: the manager fee account (78% today; its 1030 share was not
  reconstructed) and the other holders.
* **This did not happen.** No deposit or withdrawal occurred in that window (`claim_timing.json`), so
  the realized historical transfer is **0**.
* The routing check is the upper bound "every validator drained to rent + `m`, reserve to rent". The
  per-validator split of 1030 was not reconstructed. Whether the ~2.8-hour window coincided with a
  validator-capacity constraint is therefore not checked beyond this bound.

## 6. Historical realized transfers caused by late Jito credits

The only in-window user activity (epoch 1063, actor `6nk2EX…`) was reconstructed exactly:

| | Actual | If recorded first | Transfer |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Deposit `L` = 1,004,998,720 | 249,676,722 tokens | 249,676,418 | depositor +304 tokens ≈ **+1,224** lamports |
| WithdrawStake 993,739,463 tokens | 3,995,999,997 | 3,996,004,850 | withdrawer **−4,853** lamports |
| Net for the actor | | | **≈ −3,629** lamports (lost to the remaining holders) |

Across 51 epochs, total Jito revenue reaching pool stake was 8,036,936 lamports. The total realized
mis-attribution from the delay is of order 10⁴ lamports, and it went *against* the only actor who
traded in a window.

## 7. Value-transfer summary (who gains or loses from the *delay*, relative to honest recording)

| Party | Jito late credit (per epoch, live pool) | Reserve top-up (1030, hypothetical depositor `L`) |
|---|---|---|
| New depositor in window | + ≤ 0.95·z (≤ ~0.0001 SOL) MTM. Round trip negative. | + up to 13.84 SOL. The round trip is positive for every tested `L` ≥ 1 SOL (§5). Below a redemption of about 1 SOL, a validator-sourced split violates the 1-SOL minimum delegation (WITHDRAWAL_FEASIBILITY §2). |
| Withdrawer in window | − ℓ·z/(T+z) | − ℓ·a/(T+a) |
| Incumbent holders (incl. the 78% fee account) | − the depositor's gain, + the withdrawer's loss | same |
| Manager as fee recipient | 0 (L6) | 0 (L6) |
| Validator operators | 0 (their commission is fixed in the TDA) | 0 |
| Jito / external beneficiaries | 0 | 0 |
| Donor of the top-up | 0 change from timing; the donation is gone either way | same |

**Nature of the loss.** The lost value is *pool-owned revenue already credited* (`CREDITED`, not
`RECORDED`). It is not principal: no holder's previously recorded lamports are reduced. It is closest
to "unclaimed / unrecognised yield". The Jito part is negligible. The top-up part is a donation's
redistribution among holders.
